title: PSG-D2: two-level isolated records with complete online generation

claims.statement: For every integer N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, put n=ceil(log2 N). Use the single PSG-D2 algorithm and complete parameter rule in all four required proof files: psg_depth_two.md, psg_depth_two_base.md, psg_depth_two_compiler.md, psg_depth_two_budget.md. The n>=256 branch uses the exact first-feasible two-level profile, q0=(2R+1)^2, root-local Qroot=4096q0 and Wroot=4096*2^R, K=2^17n in every odd and 2-adic stage, Proot=4096n^2 and Hmax=2048K=2^28n. The n<256 branch keeps mF=2^20(n+16) and the old finite EXTRACT precision P_label_old=2^40n^4. Both branches pad actual acquisition to exactly Q=2^40n^3=1099511627776n^3. The selected full online controller is the literal construction in the compiler appendix. For every adversary in claim 5's exact adaptive model, including no corruption, it outputs the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1-2^-8>2/3. All five claims and all four bounds hold jointly on every execution branch, including failed/neutral roots, retries, discarded copies, malformed inputs, numerical errors and all padding. Constants are absolute and independent of N,s,the adversary and outcomes. Worst-case total charged sequential work is T=O(n^(7/2) (log2 n) 2^(n/4)) for n>=2, with the explicit finite n=1 branch. The equivalent positive whole-domain representative uses log2(n+2). The bound counts every classical bit operation, source cost n+1, precision, exact gate and inverse, circuit/address generation, tape/head/marker action, indexed access, initialization, measurement, reset, counter and failed work. Its exact growth index is 1.

For the same PSG-D2 algorithm and all four required proof files psg_depth_two.md, psg_depth_two_base.md, psg_depth_two_compiler.md, psg_depth_two_budget.md, for every N>=2, every s in Z/NZ and every adversary in the exact structured adaptive model, epsilon(n)=1/(8589934592n^2)=1/(2^33n^2) malformed fraction is tolerated among all Q=2^40n^3 actual acquired copies. The implied branchwise malformed count is exactly at most floor(epsilon(n)Q)=128n. Under this promise unconditional entire-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 1-2^-8>2/3 jointly with all four every-branch resource bounds in claims 1--4. The clean adversary is included, with no validity threshold. The fraction is not a per-copy independent fault rate and no maximal tolerance is asserted.

structured.error_model: Adaptive malformed-copy model with fraction epsilon(n). Parameters: N >= 2 is the modulus, s in Z/NZ the secret, n = ceil(log2 N), Q the total number of source copies the algorithm acquires, and epsilon(n) the tolerated malformed fraction. Copies are delivered one at a time in acquisition order j = 1, ..., Q. Before copy j is delivered, an adversary that knows N, s, the full description of the algorithm, and every measurement outcome the algorithm obtained before copy j is delivered, and that may hold, process and measure an arbitrary private quantum system, decides adaptively whether copy j is malformed; on every execution branch at most floor(epsilon(n) Q) of the Q acquired copies are malformed. A malformed copy is an arbitrary (n+1)-qubit state (the register shape of an ideal copy) supplied from the adversary's system: it may be pure or mixed, may be entangled with the adversary's remaining system and with other malformed copies, and may depend on all of the information above; it is not entangled with clean copies or with the algorithm's workspace, ancillas or internal random bits. Every copy that is not malformed is clean: at the moment of its delivery, a fresh ideal coset state rho_s = (1/N) sum_x |psi_{x,s}><psi_{x,s}| in tensor product with everything else (the adversary's system, all other copies and the algorithm's workspace), i.e. clean copies are independent ideal coset states. The adversary interacts with the algorithm only by supplying copies; after delivery it has no access to the copy or to the algorithm's quantum or classical systems. All measurements have countably many outcomes. The algorithm is not told which copies are malformed. Quantifiers: the guarantee must hold for every N >= 2 (no validity threshold), every s in Z/NZ and every such adversary, including the adversary that corrupts nothing (the clean problem): the algorithm outputs the entire s with probability at least 2/3, and the four declared resource bounds hold on every execution branch. The fraction bounds the number of malformed copies among acquired copies; it is not a per-copy corruption probability.
